text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated TPM on model-family 'nova-llama3x' detected in prod-us-east. 5m sustained TPM 4500 (> expected 1200). Error budget alarms firing and p95 latency > 1200ms. Paging oncall Amelia.

Amelia (oncall): Seeing the alert, joining. Can someone confirm whether this is a single-customer spike or broad? @Kevin any CS signals?

Kevin (support): Getting multiple reports from one customer (acme-corp) doing heavy batch scoring but also a handful of other noisy tenants. CX says they started a large batch job at ~12:07Z.

Jacob (sre): Running top-of-stack query for per-customer token counts. quick query: `SELECT tenant, sum(tokens) FROM requests WHERE model_family='nova-llama3x' AND ts > now()-10m GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY sum DESC LIMIT 10;` returning acme-corp ~2.8M tokens, others < 200k each.

Amelia (oncall): Okay sounds like acme-corp is dominant but we have tail noise. We should do a targeted per-model-per-tenant mitigation first (throttle their TPM) and simultaneously reduce global TPM for nova-llama3x as a safety net. Plan: 1) apply tenant carveout throttle for acme-corp 2) reduce family TPM from 1200 -> 400 3) enable overflow fallback to smaller model. 

Ash (runtime): I can apply the family change now. CLI to change per-family TPM:```
# change family rate
redwoodctl rate set --model-family nova-llama3x --tpm 400 --rpm 6000 --reason "auto-mitigation: high TPM spike 2429991111"
```

Ash (runtime): Executed. API responded 200; propagation to edge in progress (~30s). Observability: watchers on route 'generation.nova-llama3x' subscribed.

Amelia (oncall): Applying tenant throttle for acme-corp now. Using admin API to set per-tenant policy:```
PATCH /admin/tenants/acme-corp/policies
{ "policies": [{ "model_family": "nova-llama3x", "tpm": 150 }], "note": "emergency throttle - reduce noisy batch" }
```

Amelia (oncall): Tenant throttle applied. Confirmed via admin UI: acme-corp nova-llama3x tpm=150.

Jacob (sre): Early metrics: global TPM dropped from 4.5k -> 1.3k within 45s of family change and tenant throttle; p95 latency falling from 1.25s -> 680ms. No error spike on fallback.

Kevin (support): Notifying acme-corp CSM and sending a short heads-up: "We've temporarily throttled your jobs on nova-llama3x to limit impact on platform latency. Our SREs are coordinating with you to resume gradually." Lina, do we need to send an incident advisory to impacted customers?

Lina (PM): Yes please — short advisory to the customers currently experiencing higher latency and note that throttling was applied to one tenant to protect platform. Avoid over-technical language. Kevin can you draft? I'll review.

Kevin (support): Drafted advisory and posting to status: "12:10Z - We detected elevated request volume affecting generation latency for model family 'nova-llama3x'. We applied targeted throttles and reduced family throughput to stabilize latency. Some requests may experience higher queuing or reduced throughput. Engineers are monitoring."
Tried to include ETA but will wait for SRE signal.

Ash (runtime): Additional config: enabling automatic overflow route to 'nova-llama3x-quant4' (lower-cost, smaller memory) for non-critical traffic. Command:```
redwoodctl routing set --model-family nova-llama3x --overflow-model nova-llama3x-quant4 --threshold 0.85
```

Ash (runtime): Overflow enabled. Logs show a handful of switchovers, no errors in conversion.

Amelia (oncall): Monitoring dashboard: token consumption now ~900 TPM family-wide, error rate stable. Can we confirm that billing/costing alerts are not unexpectedly triggered? (we don't want to surprise finance).

Jacob (sre): Finance alerts fine, burst credits auto-deducting. I've annotated the incident with current throttles and a brief explanation. Will up the alert suppression for the family to avoid noisy paging while we observe.

Amelia (oncall): Quick risk check: any dependent customers using pinned model versions that won't accept overflow?

Ash (runtime): Good catch — two enterprise customers (zephyr-inc, delta-ops) have strict pinning to 'nova-llama3x' without overflow. I've checked their request rates; they're within normal limits under new family TPM. No action needed, but will reach out via account contacts if we plan longer reductions.

Kevin (support): Posting advisory to status page now with note about acme-corp throttle and general mitigation steps.

Lina (PM): Please add an internal note in the ticket about recommended follow-ups: 1) evaluate if acme-corp needs rate-limiting guidance / quota plan 2) consider quota policy for large batch jobs 3) post-incident review data points.

Amelia (oncall): Creating handoff summary for next oncall / SRE shift:```
- Incident start: 2429991111 (alert triggered)
- Root cause: sudden tenant batch from acme-corp & tail noise
- Actions taken: tenant throttle acme-corp -> tpm 150; family nova-llama3x tpm lowered 1200->400; overflow to quant4 enabled
- Current state: stable, TPM ~900 -> trending down; p95 latency ~680ms
- Next steps: watch for reloads, coordinate with platform-ops to craft quota guidance for acme-corp, plan possible staged ramp
- Contact: Amelia (oncall), Jacob (sre), Ash (runtime), Kevin (support)
```

Jacob (sre): I'll stay on for 15 more minutes to watch metric tails, then handover. If latency creeps above 1s again, escalate to infra and consider temporary model disable for noisy tenants.

Amelia (oncall): Noted. @oncall-next please pick up at 2429991215. I'll update the incident ticket with commands used and timestamps.

Kevin (support): I have a customer call scheduled with acme-corp in 20m; will coordinate safe ramp instructions and request they move large batch windows.

Ash (runtime): Adding a short-runbook snippet to the ticket for future oncalls: exact `redwoodctl` commands, where to check propagation, and how to revert:```
# revert family TPM
redwoodctl rate set --model-family nova-llama3x --tpm 1200 --reason "revert after stabilization"
# remove tenant policy
redwoodctl tenant policy remove --tenant acme-corp --model-family nova-llama3x
```

Amelia (oncall): Good. Closing this thread for active mitigation — will reopen if metrics regress. Leaving monitoring bookmarks. Thanks team :thumbsup:
